newsitem.title: USA: Harnischfeger seeks look at Giddings data.
newsitem.headline: Harnischfeger seeks look at Giddings data.

text.p: Harnischfeger Industries Inc said Friday it was willing to enter into a confidentiality agreement with its acquisitions target, Giddings & Lewis Inc, in order to review Giddings' financial information.
But Harnischfeger also said such an agreement should contain no restrictions, such as a "stand still" agreement that would prevent Harnischfeger from pursuing an offer without Giddings' consent.

On Thursday, Giddings said its board of directors unanimously rejected Harnischfeger's $19 a share cash tender offer for the machine tool and industrial automation products company, calling the offer inadequate.

Giddings also said it had preliminary discussions with other parties, that it had entered into confidentiality and standstill agreements with interested parties, and that it was responding to due diligence requests.
Harnischfeger quickly reiterated its plan to pursue its offer with shareholders.
Harnischfeger then said Friday it wanted to see whatever information other parties were viewing.

"As the only party willing to make any bona fide offer -- indeed, as the only party willing to state its interest in (Giddings) publicly -- we believe the (Giddings) board has a fiduciary obligation to provide Harnischfeger with the same information that is being supplied to other parties," Jeffery Grade, chief executive of mining, papermaking and material handling equipment maker Harnischfeger, said.

Harnischfeger said April 25, when it announced its offer for Giddings, that Giddings had insisted on a two-year standstill agreement before further considering a deal with Harnischfeger. Harnischfeger considered that a rejection of its offer.
Giddings could not immediately comment on Harnischfeger's request for more information.
Harnischfeger shares were up 1-1/2 at 42-1/8 Friday and Giddings shares were up 1/8 at 20-3/4.
